_comment: Which database targets the preflight is allowed to point at.
A Supabase PROJECT REF is not a secret. It is the subdomain of the public API URL and ships to every
browser as NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, so recording it here reveals nothing that is not already public.
No key, password, or connection string belongs in this file.
The list exists so 'is this production?' is answered by comparison against a recorded fact rather than
by someone reading a hostname at 2am and deciding it looks fine.

productionProjectRefs.source: Observed once in a local file on the operator machine. NOT confirmed against the authoritative source.
productionProjectRefs.note: TREATED AS PRODUCTION, UNCONFIRMED. The owner keeps environment variables in Vercel, not in local files, so the file this ref was read from may be stale and is not evidence of what production currently uses. The ref is kept here anyway because the two errors are not symmetric: wrongly refusing this target costs a re-run, wrongly allowing it could put a migration into production. It stays until the owner confirms the real production ref - at which point this entry should be corrected, not merely appended to.
productionProjectRefs.howToConfirm: The owner reads it from the Vercel project's environment settings. Do NOT go looking for it - that means reading deployment configuration, which is out of scope for this work.

_stagingNote: A target is only accepted when it can be POSITIVELY identified as staging. Absence of evidence that it is production is NOT evidence that it is staging - 'unknown' is refused, deliberately.
